addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- gitnexus-cli: Use when the user needs to run GitNexus CLI commands like analyze/index a repo, check status, clean the index, generate a wiki, or list indexed repos. Examples: "Index this repo", "Reanalyze the codebase", "Generate a wiki"
- gitnexus-debugging: Use when the user is debugging a bug, tracing an error, or asking why something fails. Examples: "Why is X failing?", "Where does this error come from?", "Trace this bug"
- gitnexus-exploring: Use when the user asks how code works, wants to understand architecture, trace execution flows, or explore unfamiliar parts of the codebase. Examples: "How does X work?", "What calls this function?", "Show me the auth flow"
- gitnexus-guide: Use when the user asks about GitNexus itself — available tools, how to query the knowledge graph, MCP resources, graph schema, or workflow reference. Examples: "What GitNexus tools are available?", "How do I use GitNexus?"
- gitnexus-impact-analysis: Use when the user wants to know what will break if they change something, or needs safety analysis before editing code. Examples: "Is it safe to change X?", "What depends on this?", "What will break?"
- gitnexus-pdg-query: Use when querying or extending GitNexus's PDG control/data-dependence surface (the `pdg_query` MCP tool, CDG/REACHING_DEF edges), or reasoning about "what controls X" / "where does Y flow" / guard clauses. Examples: "what guards this statement?", "trace this variable within the function", "why is the pdg_query result empty?", "add a CDG query".
- gitnexus-pr-review: Use when the user wants to review a pull request, understand what a PR changes, assess risk of merging, or check for missing test coverage. Examples: "Review this PR", "What does PR #42 change?", "Is this PR safe to merge?"
- gitnexus-refactoring: Use when the user wants to rename, extract, split, move, or restructure code safely. Examples: "Rename this function", "Extract this into a module", "Refactor this class", "Move this to a separate file"
- gitnexus-taint-analysis: Use when working on, reviewing, or extending GitNexus's CFG/taint/PDG subsystem (the `--pdg` layers), or when reasoning about source→sink data-flow findings. Examples: "How does taint analysis work here?", "Why didn't explain find this flow?", "Add a new sink/source", "Review the interprocedural taint code".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I now have a comprehensive picture. Let me compile the findings.

Here is the complete report of all server-side enforcement sites for memo visibility in this repository.

---

## Visibility Model

The visibility enum is defined in `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go` (lines 12-22):
- `Public` ("PUBLIC") -- visible to everyone
- `Protected` ("PROTECTED") -- visible to any authenticated user
- `Private` ("PRIVATE") -- visible only to the memo creator (and admins)

---

## 1. Central Read-Access Gate

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`
**Function:** `checkMemoReadAccess` (lines 39-68)

This is the primary reusable enforcement function. Logic:
- Archived memos: only visible to their creator (line 45-53).
- Non-PUBLIC memos require authentication; anonymous callers get `Unauthenticated` (lines 55-62).
- PRIVATE memos: only the creator may view; others get `PermissionDenied` (line 63-64). Note: unlike other sites, this function does NOT grant admin bypass for PRIVATE memos.

Called from:
- `GetMemo` at line 356 (on the memo itself) and line 367 (on the parent memo if it is a comment).
- `ListMemoComments` at line 148 of `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`.

---

## 2. List Memos (Query-Time Filtering)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`
**Function:** `ListMemos` (lines 178-227)

Visibility is enforced at query time via `VisibilityList` and CEL filter expressions before the database query runs:
- **Anonymous caller** (line 218-219): `VisibilityList` set to `[Public]` only.
- **Authenticated, listing all creators** (lines 221-223): CEL filter `creator_id == {currentUser.ID} || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` -- the user sees their own memos of any visibility plus PUBLIC/PROTECTED memos from others.
- **Authenticated, listing another user's memos** (lines 224-225): `VisibilityList` set to `[Public, Protected]`.
- **Archived memos** (lines 188-196): restricted to `CreatorID = currentUser.ID`; anonymous callers get an empty response.

---

## 3. ListMemoComments Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`
**Function:** `ListMemoComments` (lines 136-161)

After checking `checkMemoReadAccess` on the parent memo (line 148), comment listing applies its own visibility filter:
- Anonymous caller (line 157-158): filter `visibility == "PUBLIC"`.
- Authenticated caller (line 160): filter `creator_id == {currentUser.ID} || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.

---

## 4. CreateMemoComment Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`
**Function:** `CreateMemoComment` (lines 20-43)

Before allowing a comment, checks that the parent memo is not private to someone else (line 41):
```go
if relatedMemo.Visibility == store.Private && relatedMemo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
    return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
}
```

---

## 5. Reaction Service Visibility Checks

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`

Three separate enforcement points:

- **`ListMemoReactions`** (lines 29-41): Inline visibility check -- non-PUBLIC requires auth; PRIVATE requires creator or admin.
- **`UpsertMemoReaction`** (lines 82-85): Checks PRIVATE visibility before allowing a reaction upsert.
- **`DeleteMemoReaction`** (lines 126-139): Ownership check on the reaction itself (not directly visibility, but prevents revealing existence of private memos' reactions).

---

## 6. Memo Attachment Visibility Checks

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`
**Function:** `ListMemoAttachments` (lines 200-225)

Inline visibility check (lines 213-224): non-PUBLIC requires auth; PRIVATE requires creator or admin.

---

## 7. Attachment Service - checkAttachmentAccess

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`
**Function:** `checkAttachmentAccess` (lines 419-455)

For attachments linked to a memo, visibility follows the memo's rules (lines 445-453):
- PUBLIC: access granted.
- Non-PUBLIC: requires auth.
- PRIVATE: requires creator or admin.

Called from `GetAttachment` at line 256.

---

## 8. File Server - checkAttachmentPermission

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
**Function:** `checkAttachmentPermission` (lines 649-704)

This is the HTTP file-serving path (not gRPC). It enforces memo visibility with additional nuances:
- Unlinked attachments: creator-only access (lines 651-663).
- PUBLIC memo on an open instance (`AllowAnonymous()`): served anonymously (line 677).
- **Share token fallback** (lines 684-688): If the request carries a valid, non-expired `share_token` for the memo, access is granted even for private/protected memos.
- Authenticated access: PRIVATE requires the creator or admin role (line 699).

---

## 9. User Stats Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`

Two functions enforce visibility when computing statistics:

- **`ListAllUserStats`** (lines 77-91): Anonymous sees only PUBLIC; authenticated user listing another user sees PUBLIC + PROTECTED; listing all creators uses CEL filter.
- **`GetUserStats`** (lines 217-221): Anonymous sees only PUBLIC; authenticated user viewing another user sees PUBLIC + PROTECTED.

---

## 10. RSS Feed - Public-Only Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go`

- **`GetSystemRSS`** (line 90): `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- only PUBLIC memos in system RSS.
- **`GetUserRSS`** (line 141): `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- only PUBLIC memos in per-user RSS.

---

## 11. Frontend / Sitemap - Public-Only Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`
**Function:** `getSitemapXML` (line 150)

Only PUBLIC memos appear in the sitemap:
```go
VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public},
```

---

## 12. SSE Hub - canReceive

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`
**Function:** `canReceive` (lines 134-144)

Filters which SSE events each connected client receives based on the event's visibility:
- PRIVATE: only the creator or admin role receives the event.
- PUBLIC / PROTECTED / empty: all authenticated clients receive it.
- Unknown visibility: denied with a warning log.

SSE events carry visibility via the `SSEEvent.Visibility` field (set in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go`).

---

## 13. SSE Handler - Authentication Gate

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`
**Function:** `handleSSE` (lines 34-44)

Requires authentication (Bearer token) before subscribing to SSE events. Anonymous connections are rejected with 401.

---

## 14. Notification Visibility Guards

### 14a. User Notification Conversion

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`
**Function:** `canViewerAccessMemo` (lines 302-316)

Helper used to suppress notification payloads the viewer should not see:
- Admin: always allowed.
- PRIVATE: only the creator.
- PROTECTED: any authenticated viewer.
- PUBLIC: everyone.

Called from:
- `convertMemoCommentNotificationPayload` (lines 337, 342)
- `convertMemoMentionNotificationPayload` (lines 370, 385)

### 14b. Email Notification Visibility

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/notification/email.go`
**Function:** `canViewerAccessMemo` (lines 306-320) -- a duplicate of the same logic.

Called from:
- `buildMemoCommentEmailMessage` (line 155)
- `buildMemoMentionEmailMessage` (line 187)

Both suppress email notifications when the receiver cannot access the memo.

---

## 15. Mention Helpers - Visibility Gating

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`
**Function:** `canUserAccessMentionContext` (lines 56-71)

Checks whether a mentioned user can access the memo context:
- If `relatedMemo` is PRIVATE and the target is not its creator, access is denied.
- If the `memo` itself is PRIVATE and the target is not its creator, access is denied.

Called from `shouldSkipMentionInbox` (line 88), which prevents creating inbox items for memos the target user cannot view.

---

## 16. Memo Share Service - Share Token Access Path

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go`
**Function:** `GetMemoByShare` (lines 151-192)

Provides an alternate access path that bypasses normal visibility checks: a valid, non-expired share token grants read access to any memo regardless of visibility. Archived memos are still hidden (line 164).

---

## 17. ACL Configuration & Auth Interceptors

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`

Defines which memo endpoints are publicly accessible (lines 32-41):
- `GetMemo`, `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, `GetMemoByShare` are marked public -- but the service layer enforces visibility filtering internally.

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/authz.go`
**Function:** `CheckAccess` (lines 58-69)

The `Authorizer` enforces method-level access: non-public methods require authentication; on a private instance, only the auth-bootstrap set is accessible anonymously.

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`
**Function:** `AuthInterceptor.WrapUnary` (lines 217-231)

The Connect transport interceptor that delegates to `Authorizer` for every RPC call.

---

## 18. Store-Level Query Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/memo.go` (lines 96-102)
**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/memo.go` (lines 89-95)
**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/memo.go` (same pattern)

All three database drivers translate `FindMemo.VisibilityList` into a SQL `WHERE memo.visibility IN (...)` clause, ensuring visibility filtering happens at the database level.

**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/filter/schema.go` (lines 162-166, 241)

The CEL filter engine exposes `visibility` as a filterable field mapped to `memo.visibility`, supporting expressions like `visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` that are compiled into SQL WHERE clauses.

---

## Summary Table

| # | File | Function/Site | What It Enforces |
|---|------|--------------|------------------|
| 1 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39` | `checkMemoReadAccess` | Central gate: archived=creator-only; non-PUBLIC=auth required; PRIVATE=creator-only |
| 2 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227` | `ListMemos` | Query-time visibility filtering by user context |
| 3 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:148,157-160` | `ListMemoComments` | Parent-memo read check + comment visibility filter |
| 4 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41` | `CreateMemoComment` | PRIVATE parent memo blocks non-creator comments |
| 5 | `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30,83` | `ListMemoReactions`, `UpsertMemoReaction` | Visibility check before reaction operations |
| 6 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214` | `ListMemoAttachments` | Non-PUBLIC requires auth; PRIVATE=creator/admin |
| 7 | `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422` | `checkAttachmentAccess` | Linked attachment follows memo visibility |
| 8 | `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650` | `checkAttachmentPermission` | HTTP file serving: memo visibility + share-token fallback |
| 9 | `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84,90,218,220` | `ListAllUserStats`, `GetUserStats` | Visibility-filtered memo counting |
| 10 | `server/router/rss/rss.go:90,141` | `GetSystemRSS`, `GetUserRSS` | PUBLIC-only for RSS feeds |
| 11 | `server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150` | `getSitemapXML` | PUBLIC-only for sitemap |
| 12 | `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134` | `SSEClient.canReceive` | PRIVATE events only to creator/admin |
| 13 | `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:34` | `handleSSE` | SSE requires authentication |
| 14a | `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:302` | `canViewerAccessMemo` | Suppresses notifications for inaccessible memos |
| 14b | `server/notification/email.go:306` | `canViewerAccessMemo` | Suppresses email notifications for inaccessible memos |
| 15 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:56` | `canUserAccessMentionContext` | Prevents mention inbox for PRIVATE memos |
| 16 | `server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:151` | `GetMemoByShare` | Bypass path via share token (skips visibility) |
| 17 | `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` + `authz.go` + `connect_interceptors.go:217` | `PublicMethods`, `CheckAccess`, `AuthInterceptor` | Method-level auth gating; public memo endpoints allow anonymous but defer to service-layer visibility |
| 18 | `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/memo.go` + `internal/filter/schema.go` | SQL `WHERE visibility IN (...)` | Database-level enforcement of `VisibilityList` |
